title: style: Frontend-Design-Überarbeitung v2 (Ember/Gold-Ticket-Motiv)
context: Direct user feedback that an earlier design pass looked generic (matched a cliché pattern flagged by Anthropic's own frontend-design skill guidance), followed by a second round of feedback that the resulting layout looked like a mobile banking app rather than a website. Two mockups were shown for approval; the second (dark warm-gradient hero, tab-style category nav, 3-column card grid) was explicitly approved by the user before implementation.

review_findings.reason: Hero gradient hex colors (#2b1c14/#4a2e1c) were hardcoded ad-hoc in 4 page files instead of design tokens, and all 4 corresponding a11y test files independently re-declared the same hex literal instead of importing the real token value -- the contrast tests never observed the actual implementation.

Multi-variant dish card's <summary> disclosure trigger had its accessible name fully overridden by an aria-label that excluded the price, and focus-visible styling was applied to a decorative aria-hidden span instead of the actual focusable <summary>.
5 admin UI files were touched (legitimate link-color-scheme-safety migration + a publish-panel bugfix) but not documented as in-scope in the PR description.
New lucide-react dependency (ISC-licensed) not recorded in docs/platform/service-register.md's permissive-license list.
New order-status ticket-stamp order-number badge had no test coverage.

required_actions: Promote hero gradient colors to real design tokens, used in all 4 pages, referenced (not restated) by the 4 a11y tests.
Fix the disclosure trigger's accessible name to include the price; move focus-visible to the actual focusable element.
Document the 5 touched admin files in the PR description.
Add a test for the order-number badge.
cycles.resolved_by: commits addressing all 5 findings, pushed to chore/frontend-design-overhaul-v2

review_findings.reason: Sold-out dish cards applied a blanket opacity-60 to their entire text block, dimming the description AND the legally-relevant allergen notice to ~2.77:1 contrast -- below the 4.5:1 AA minimum. This was a genuine regression introduced by the cycle-1 repair's broader (owner-directed) layout rebuild, not present on main before this PR.
Sold-out dishes no longer displayed a price at all (only available on main previously) -- the price render was fully gated behind `!dish.soldOut`.

Two additional scope items (dark-mode removal fixing a real invisible-text bug; the public-menu layout rebuild responding to direct owner feedback) were introduced during repair cycles without being explicitly documented as their own scope items.
Dark-mode removal's globals.css comment said 'tracked as a follow-up' with no actual issue created anywhere.

The 4 hero-contrast a11y tests asserted against the DARKER gradient stop (espresso-900) as the stated 'worst case' for light text on a dark background -- inverted; the lighter stop (espresso-800) is actually the worst case for that direction.

required_actions: Remove the opacity-60 dimming from sold-out card text; rely on the existing solid badge + grayed placeholder for sold-out signalling.
Restore price display for sold-out dishes; only suppress the add/chooser control.
Document the dark-mode removal and layout rebuild as explicit scope items in the PR description.
Open a real GitHub issue for the dark-mode-reactivation follow-up and reference it by number.
Fix the hero-contrast tests to assert against the lighter/worse-case gradient stop.
cycles.resolved_by: final repair commit, pushed to chore/frontend-design-overhaul-v2 (head 1a1c759)

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Sold-out card no longer blanket-dims text; real contrast assertion added
acceptance_criteria.evidence: opacity-60 removed from the dish-card text wrapper; public-menu-design.a11y.test.ts asserts the actual rendered neutral-500/neutral-0 pair passes AA, plus keeps an inverted regression test proving the old opacity-60 composite would fail. DOM-level test confirms no opacity-* class on the description/allergen-notice elements.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Sold-out dishes show price again; only add control suppressed
acceptance_criteria.evidence: dish-card.tsx renders formatPrice/startingPriceLabel for sold-out dishes with no add button or chooser disclosure; covered by new tests.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: PR description documents dark-mode removal and layout rebuild as explicit scope items
acceptance_criteria.evidence: PR body's 'Zusätzliche Scope-Items' section covers both with rationale and commit references.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Real tracking issue exists for dark-mode reactivation, referenced by number
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Issue #83 created and open; globals.css comment references it explicitly.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Hero-contrast tests use the correct worst-case gradient stop
acceptance_criteria.evidence: All 4 *-design.a11y.test.ts files now assert against colors.espresso[800] with corrected reasoning in comments; white text still passes AA with a wide margin.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No new regressions; final commit scope contained; earlier cycle fixes intact
acceptance_criteria.evidence: 8 files, +169/-45 in the final commit, all attributable to the 5 findings. Cycle-1/2 fixes verified still present (no text-brand-600, espresso tokens intact, lucide-react license recorded, disclosure aria-label/focus-visible fix intact).

review_findings.reason: The visible price label differs between sold-out ("ab 8,90 €") and available ("8,90 €", with "ab" only in the aria-label) multi-variant dish cards.
review_findings.required_correction: Optional follow-up: use startingPriceLabel's visible text consistently in both states.
review_findings.outcome: not required for merge, deferred as optional polish

residual_risks: Contrast coverage is token-level + DOM-class assertions, not rendered-pixel verification.
Automatic OS dark mode remains disabled repo-wide pending the issue #83 audit.
No integration/e2e checks configured for this UI-only PR; verified at unit/DOM level only.
